# Job Chapter 27 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 425v–426r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOB_027_page_001.jpg, JOB_027_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Job continued his speech:

**2** "I swear by the living God, who has denied me justice — by the Almighty, who has filled my soul with bitterness —

**3** that as long as I have breath in my body, as long as God's spirit fills my lungs,

**4** my lips will never speak a lie, and my tongue will never utter deceit.

**5** I will never concede that you are right! Until the day I die, I will not surrender my integrity.

**6** I will hold tight to my innocence and never let go; my conscience does not condemn me for a single day of my life.

**7** May my enemies suffer the fate of the wicked; may those who oppose me receive what the unrighteous deserve.

**8** For what hope does a godless person have when God cuts him off and takes away his life?

**9** Will God listen to his cry when disaster strikes?

**10** Will he find delight in the Almighty? Will he call on God when times are hard?

**11** I will teach you about God's power; I will not hide what the Almighty has in store.

**12** Look — you have all witnessed these things yourselves! So why do you keep talking such nonsense?

**13** Here is what God has in store for the wicked, the inheritance oppressors receive from the Almighty:

**14** Even if his children are many, they are destined for the sword; his descendants will never have enough to eat.

**15** Those who survive him will be buried by plague, and their widows will shed no tears.

**16** Even if he stockpiles silver like dirt and hoards clothing like stacks of clay —

**17** he may collect it, but the righteous will wear it, and the innocent will divide his silver.

**18** The house he builds is as fragile as a moth's cocoon, as flimsy as a watchman's temporary shelter.

**19** He goes to bed wealthy, but wakes to find it all gone — he opens his eyes and everything has vanished.

**20** Terrors wash over him like a flood; a storm sweeps him away in the night.

**21** The scorching east wind snatches him up and carries him off, hurling him from his place.

**22** It strikes him down without mercy; he tries desperately to flee from its force.

**23** It claps its hands in mockery and hisses him out of his place."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**v.2 — The impossible oath:** Job swears by the God who has wronged him. This is not a contradiction — it reveals the depth of Job's faith. He has no other God to swear by. Even in his rage, he cannot escape the relationship.

**v.5 — The heart of the book:** "I will not surrender my integrity" — this single declaration is the spine of the entire Book of Job. God himself affirmed Job's integrity in 1:8 and 2:3; now Job refuses to abandon what God declared true, even when God seems to have abandoned him.

**vv.13-23 — Whose theology is this?:** These verses sound remarkably like the friends' retribution theology. Many scholars believe this section originally belonged to Zophar's undelivered third speech. But in its current form, Job may be saying: "I know the standard theology about the wicked — and it does not apply to my case."

*— PNEUMA*
